correctness.rationale: For all finite connected simple H of n≥2 vertices, direct proof shows successful skew forcing iff the initial set contains an original vertex and its unselected edge-subdivision vertices form a forest. Leaf deletion and connectivity give a constructive forcing process. Forest edge count yields exactly B(r,T) rooted-tree minima, the Tutte polynomial transform, and a K_n Cartesian product with spanning-tree exchange graph under token jumping. The fundamental-cycle exchange argument proves the exact all-pairs metric; original/subdivision bipartiteness makes every optimum slide invalid. In complete graphs, the degree is W(T) by fundamental cycle lengths, and Cayley shore splitting yields the closed edge count; edge-disjoint spanning trees prove sharp diameter. All boundaries n=2,3 are treated. The 47-graph exhaustive forcing test and Prüfer checks through K7 succeeded on the packaged paths; finite tests are corroboration not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Claimed originality is the all-source-graph optimum reconfiguration product and its exact shortest-path metric, plus complete-graph Wiener degree, closed exchange-edge count and sharp diameter. The forest criterion follows as a specialization of Bonato et al. 2024 Theorem 33 combined with the leaf criterion and is not asserted independently novel. The tree-only slide statement is covered by Bong et al. 2025. DeAlba 2014 treats restricted bipartite uniquely restricted matchings and the indexed ordinary full-subdivision record uses a different forcing rule. Distinct nearby Wiener formulas concern other parameters. Title/summary-only historical indexing and unindexed equivalent results remain risks.
residual_risks: A general 2024 incidence/lazy-burning theorem already implies the feasibility criterion; originality cannot rest on this criterion alone.
The 2025 tree theorem covers the case of tree subdivisions under token sliding; priority claims concern the full family and the exchange product and enumeration.
Only indexed summaries, not complete text, were available for two relevant published records; an unindexed equivalent proof or table remains possible.
The existing Cayley tree count is known; novelty is not asserted for that integer sequence or for generic spanning-tree basis connectivity.

value.rationale: The same source graph H controls a natural network of optimal skew-forcing seeds via its spanning-tree basis exchange graph, with exact minimum-cardinality paths and a sharp obstruction to any adjacency-constrained relocation. The Tutte transform counts all feasible sets, not just optima; the clique family has the exact all-order Wiener degree law, total transition count and diameter n. These structural facts connect propagation, matroid bases, network relocation and classical tree distance invariants; they are not arbitrary small-instance numerics or a restatement of the forcing-number bound.
